Standard Operating Procedure — SOA Generation

Advice Request Builder → Smart Drop → SOA Generator → Word export  ·  interactive training guide with live screenshots

This SOP takes you from a finished strategy meeting to a draft SOA in Word. Click any screenshot to zoom. Tick the checklists as you work — your progress is saved in this browser. Every step of this process keeps a person in control: nothing is applied to the SOA without your confirmation, and everything the tools can't resolve is flagged for you rather than guessed.

Who this is for. This SOP is written for the associate producing the SOA. The adviser makes the advice decisions at the strategy meeting and signs off the final document; the associate operates the toolchain and prepares the draft.

1

Complete the Advice Request Builder

▾

Open MWS_Advice_Request_Builder_4.html in your browser. The builder is the single source of truth for what this SOA recommends — everything you tick here arrives in the SOA with the firm's approved wording attached.

There is no autosave in this builder — 💾 Save your work regularly. Four buttons manage your file: 💾 Save downloads a full working-state file (advice_request_state.json) you can reopen later; ⬆ Load reloads a saved state file back into the form so you can keep editing; ⬇ .json exports advice_request.json — this is the file the generator imports; and ⬇ Download Word produces the human-readable advice request for the client file. Save/Load is for resuming your own editing; the ⬇ .json export is what feeds the generator. Always check the strategy ticks are present before exporting: an advice request exported with no ticks produces an SOA with derived super/insurance wording only, and the generator flags it loudly in the attention list.

  1. Header & Clients — Single/Joint, New/Existing, adviser, client first name(s). The "Hi Team" narrative is free text for the associate and is also keyword-scanned.
  2. Entities — add any SMSF, company, bucket company or family trust with its name and ABN/ACN. These flow to the SOA's entity fields, ownership labels and the Entity Strategies section.
  3. Risk Profile — per client and per entity. If you're bumping a profile (e.g. Growth → High Growth), record it here — the SOA's bump wording comes from this.
  4. Scope — untick any area that is out of scope, and tick the scope-out reasons. Unticked areas are blanked in the SOA and listed in "Scope of our Advice".
  5. Strategy ticks — work through each in-scope area. Fill every $ slot and pick every dropdown choice; a slot you leave blank arrives in the SOA as $XXX for the associate to chase. Not sure which tick? See the Option guide below.
  6. Products & fees — recommended super platform, recommended insurer per client, and the fee matrix (flat or % of balance). The fee tables in the SOA are computed from exactly what you enter here.
Export both formats when you're done: ⬇ .json (the file the generator reads) and ⬇ Download Word (the human-readable copy for the client file). The topbar also has ⧉ Copy for pasting the text version into an email or task.

2

Gather the supporting documents

▾

Collect everything below that exists for the client. You will drop the whole set onto the generator in one go — order doesn't matter, the generator applies them in a safe fixed sequence.

Step 2 checklist

3

Open the generator and set the SOA type

▾

Open SOA_Generator_v190_38r.html. You land on Import Data. Before importing anything, set the SOA type — it drives the goals, summaries and projected-outcome wording throughout the document.

  • Wealth accumulation SOA — full goal set including budgeting.
  • Retirement SOA — retirement goals; budgeting goal removed across goals, summaries and projections; pension/transfer wording enabled.

Step 3 checklist

4

Smart drop — import everything in one batch

▾

Drag the whole document set into the ⚡ Smart drop zone (or click Choose files…). Every file is read and identified, and each per-person document is matched to its client from the document content and filename. Nothing applies until you confirm.

Apply order is fixed and safe regardless of how you dropped: word bank → fact-find → Advice Request → data collection → CARE → WealthSolver → Risk Researcher → quotes → existing cover → commissions. Identity always loads before per-person documents; premiums always exist before commission maths.

Same build, same SOA — reproducibility. The SOA is a pure function of the set of files you drop, not the order or the number of drags — so any two associates on the same build produce the identical document. Keep these in mind:

  • Everyone runs the SAME build. Check the version stamp shown in the toolbar (MWS_GEN_VERSION, currently v190_38r) — it is also written into every exported Word doc's properties (File ▸ Info ▸ Properties). Confirm it matches across the team before comparing drafts; a mismatch means someone is still on an old copy, so re-download the canonical build.
  • Drop in any order, in one batch or several. Every drop accumulates into one running set, and the whole set is re-ordered and re-applied into the correct sequence automatically — upload order and the number of drags never change the result, and a re-dropped file simply replaces its earlier version.
  • Every fresh generation starts from a clean slate. Dropping the fact-find / advice request resets the state first, so leftover data from a previous client can't bleed in. Even so, click ↺ Reset (or reload) before starting a new client, and make any manual edits after your final drop.
  • Multi-account super replacement table: when a client has more than one existing super account, the per-fund Administration / Investment management / ICR cells are intentionally left blank for you to enter manually. A single existing account still auto-fills from WealthSolver.
Read the completion report. It lists every file applied (and to whom), anything skipped, importer warnings, and the "still needs your attention" list. Don't dismiss it without reading — it is the map of what to fix in step 5.
A file shows "type not recognised"? Set its type manually in the modal — or leave it as Skip and enter that data by hand in step 6. A skipped file is always listed in the report; nothing disappears silently.

Step 4 checklist

5

Resolve gaps and conflicts

▾

The generator flags what it couldn't resolve, in three places:

  1. The attention list (in the completion report): strategies with no word-bank match, unrecognised areas, and key figures that came through empty (balances, premiums, fees).
  2. The Data conflicts panel (top of the editor): mismatches between what the SOA scopes and what the Wealth Projector modelled — each with severity and an explanation of which source wins.
  3. CARE balance reconciliation (in the conflicts panel): each person's CARE doc super amount must equal their current super balance − retained minimum on the existing fund − upfront super fee (a CARE doc modelled before the fee deduction also reconciles). A mismatch names the person and shows both expected figures next to the CARE amount.
  4. In-document placeholders: unresolved figures print as $XXX and unresolved wording choices as yellow-highlighted brackets — impossible to miss in the preview or the export.
Fast placeholder sweep: use the browser's find (Ctrl+F) over the preview for $XXX and [ to find every remaining placeholder in seconds.

Step 5 checklist

6

Review and edit section by section

▾

Work down the left sidebar — Setup, Front matter, then the Advice sections. Active sections show a tick; sections outside scope are greyed. Clicking a section opens its editor in the middle and scrolls the live preview to the same place on the right.

  • Every field is editable. The word-bank wording is a starting point, not a cage — adjust any sentence for the client's circumstances.
  • Per-section controls: ↺ Reset section restores the standard wording; ✕ Remove from SOA deactivates the section (it can be re-activated from the sidebar).
  • Couples: check both clients' bands appear in the product, replacement, comparison and asset-allocation tables. A missing client means their source document didn't import — go back to step 4 rather than typing their data by hand.
  • Undo/redo are in the topbar; the session auto-saves. Save copy exports your working state.

Step 6 checklist

7

Export to Word and finalise

▾

Click ⬇ Export Word in the topbar. The .docx downloads locally — nothing is uploaded anywhere. The export runs the same safety nets as the preview, so the document matches what you reviewed.

Final pre-release checklist

Remember: the export is a draft. The standard review process is unchanged — this tool gets you a consistent, complete draft faster; it does not sign off advice.

Option guide — when to select X over Y

▾

The most common judgement calls in the builder, area by area. These are prompts, not rules — the adviser's strategy meeting decision always wins.

Client framing — new vs existing, reference by incorporation
Select…When…
New clientFirst SOA with the firm. Full introduction and current-situation build.
Existing clientAny further advice. Uses the review/enhancement opener and the "risk profile remains appropriate" wording where you confirm it.
Reference by incorporationAn area (e.g. estate planning) was covered in a prior SOA and isn't being re-advised — cite the prior SOA date instead of scoping it in.
1 · Debt Management
Select…Over…When…
Utilise offsetEstablish offsetThe client already has an offset facility; "Establish" only when one must be opened.
Direct surplus income to offsetDirect tax savings to offsetSurplus = regular cashflow; tax savings = the annual refund generated by the strategy set. Often both.
Refinance P&I → interest onlyKeep P&ICashflow is being redirected to a higher-priority strategy (usually gearing/investment) and the loan is investment-related or the IO period is deliberate. Note the equity build trade-off.
GEARING ticks (equity release / term loan / debt recycling)Cash-funded investingUsable equity + reliable surplus + long horizon + risk profile that supports leverage. These ticks trigger the firm's full gearing wording: 14-item risk set and the loan-limit table.
Consolidate car loan / other debtLeave debts separateHigh-interest consumer debt exists and home-loan consolidation genuinely lowers cost — pair with closing the facility to prevent re-accumulation.
Set aside funds for home sale & purchase (PPR)Investing those fundsA PPR transaction is imminent; funds are quarantined, and no property advice is being given.
4 · Investment Plan — funding method is the big decision
Select…Over…When…
100% lump sum investedDCASmaller amounts, funds already market-exposed, or time-in-market is the priority and the client is comfortable with immediate full exposure.
DCA — % upfront, remainder over 12 months100% lump sumLarge lump sums (inheritance, sale proceeds) and/or a client sensitive to investing at a peak. Record the upfront %.
MOTM framework (overlay)Plain fixed-schedule DCATick with DCA when the firm's Money-on-the-Move overlay applies: for every 5% market fall, a month of DCA is brought forward. This is the house default for staged investment.
In-specie transfer (either tick)Sell down & repurchaseExisting holdings can move to the new platform without sale — minimises buy/sell spread, time out of market, and avoids crystallising CGT. Use the CGT free-text tick when a partial sale is still needed.
Add a reserves portfolioFully growth-investedThe client will draw an income (retirement or drawdown tick): reserves fund the drawdown in a downturn so growth assets aren't sold at lows.
Commence drawdown—The investment will pay the client an income. Pair with reserves; check the SOA type is Retirement if this is retirement income.
Vanguard index optionCARE managed portfoliosCost sensitivity or client preference for passive; otherwise CARE is the default and carries the philosophy justification modules.
5 · Personal Superannuation
Select…Over…When…
Full rollover (close & transfer 100%)Partial rolloverNothing needs to stay behind. WealthSolver comparison supports the move.
Partial — retain minimum for insuranceFull rolloverExisting fund insurance is being kept (can't be replaced on equal terms) — retain the minimum balance that keeps the cover alive.
Partial — retain minimum for SG contributionsFull rolloverEmployer contributions keep flowing to the old fund (e.g. award/defined arrangements).
Retain existing fundRolloverThe comparison doesn't justify moving — invest in line with the risk profile where the fund allows.
MOTM / DCA / 100% lump sum (super variants)each otherSame logic as the Investment Plan funding decision, applied to the rollover amount.
CGT applicable within super—Always tick when a rollover/rebalance will realise gains inside the fund — it inserts the caution wording so the client isn't surprised by the fund-level tax.
Apply for Centrelink Age Pension—Retirement trigger reached and eligibility likely — inserts the application recommendation.
SMSF ticksRetail fund ticksPer the strategy meeting. SMSF wording lives here (not in the Entities card) — the Entities card captures the fund's legal details.

Defined-benefit funds: Military Super (and similar) is split automatically — the Member & Ancillary portion is rolled over, while the Defined-Benefit / Employer portion is scoped out and retained.

6 · Superannuation Contributions

Superannuation Contributions is a sub-category of Personal Superannuation: in the builder it sits indented under the super area, and in the generated SOA the contribution recommendations are combined into the Superannuation section (no separate “Superannuation Contributions” heading).

Select…When…
Salary sacrifice / concessionalPre-tax capacity within the cap; employer facilitates. Use "Arrange salary sacrifice with employer" for the mechanics tick.
Carry-forward concessionalUnused cap from prior years + total super balance under the threshold. Use the CGT-offset variant when the contribution is timed against an asset-sale gain.
Non-concessional / bring-forwardAfter-tax lump sums; bring-forward for amounts above one year's cap.
Spouse contribution / co-contribution / contribution splittingLow-income spouse (tax offset), low-income co-contribution eligibility, or balance-equalisation strategies.
Notes (work test, Div 293, Div 296)Tick whenever the client's age/income/balance makes them relevant — they insert the caution wording only.
7 · Personal Protection
Select…Over…When…
Take out new coverTop-up existingNo adequate existing cover, or replacement is recommended. "Replace / cancel & take out new" when old policies end.
Retain employer paid coverReplace itThe employer funds it — free cover is kept. Use the + top up variant when it's kept but insufficient, and new personal cover fills the gap.
Own-occupation TPDAny-occupationSpecialised occupation where "any occupation" would under-protect; premiums are higher. "Differentiate by life stage" splits own-occ for the primary earner / any-occ for the spouse.
Only eligible for Any-occ / Non-occ / Homemaker TPDthe preferred definitionUnderwriting reality: the client's occupation/duties (or homemaker status) limits the definition available. The tick inserts the explanation of the limitation.
Zurich Active (health-events cover)Traditional Life / TPD / TraumaThe client is not eligible for TPD / Income Protection (e.g. limited work hours). The generator then produces the Active health-events cover, the super/cash premium split, and the specific Zurich Active wording.
IP increasing claims (CPI)Level claimsTick the standard CPI tick where available; tick CPI not available when the product can't offer it, so the SOA explains the limitation instead of staying silent.
Dual income protection (retail top-up over employer/industry)Single policyEmployer/industry IP exists but is capped — retail top-up with offset wording.
Pre-assessment factors — smoker / health / pastimes—Tick each factor disclosed at pre-assessment that affects terms (loadings, exclusions). The SOA then explains why quoted terms differ from standard rates.
IP affordability structuringDefault 30-day/age-65Waiting and benefit periods calibrated to leave balances and cash buffer to bring the premium into budget.

One template for every insurer: the insurance products, strategies and comparison tables now render from a single firm-standard template regardless of insurer. The existing-cover increase quotes populate the (Existing Increased) comparison rows.

New in v190_38r (Rounds 15–19): insurance products now match the firm's ROA layout across insurers (ClearView annual-super premium calc; OnePath OneCare super/personal split; AustralianSuper existing-increase row); the single-existing-fund replacement table renders 3 columns; advice-request insurance benefits render only in the "Why" band; and a "Cancel" insurance action drives cancel-and-replace. Rounds 17–19 add same-build reproducibility (a visible toolbar/Word-doc build stamp, an order-independent smart drop that re-applies the whole file set from a clean slate, and a clean-slate reset on each fresh generation) plus the multi-account super replacement table (per-fund fee cells left blank for manual entry) — see the reproducibility note in Step 4.

8 · Cashflow, 2 · Property, 3 · Bonds, Entities
Select…When…
MCMA cash hub vs MCAA (Accelerator)MCMA as the standard hub; MCAA where the higher-rate accelerator account fits the cash strategy.
Set aside $X for insurance costsOnly when there are no other ongoing plan costs to bundle the premiums with.
Property ticksMatch the transaction (buy with equity vs cash, sell-and-buy, convert home, retain, sell). Purchases pair with the debt-management gearing ticks.
Investment bondLong-horizon tax-paid structure (estate/minor purposes); the CGT free-text tick covers exit implications.
Entities cardEnter every advice entity (SMSF/company/trust) with full name + ABN/ACN. Company/trust entities get their wording in the Entity Strategies section automatically; SMSF wording comes from the super ticks.

MCMA cross-check: the MCMA's insurance and investment components are reconciled against the quotes — if they look transposed, the generator fires a warning.

✎

Updating the wording (word bank)

▾

All tailored wording lives in SOA_Words_MasterList.json (163 modules; the Word version of the masterlist is generated from it). To change wording you never edit the tools:

  1. Edit the module in the masterlist JSON — reword the recommendation/why/risks/alternatives, add a module (key it "Area::Tick name" exactly as the builder names it), or delete one.
  2. Have the change reviewed the same way as any advice-wording change.
  3. Drop the JSON onto the generator's Smart drop. It's recognised as Word bank / masterlist and applied first in the batch. The report shows exactly how many modules were added / updated / removed.
  • Full masterlist file → replaces the live bank (removals take effect). Small fragment (just the modules you're changing, flat "Area::Name" keys) → merges.
  • A word-bank file can never be mistaken for client data — even mislabelled, it routes to the wording merge, not the client importer.
  • New builder ticks must get a matching masterlist module (same area + name), or the tick will import as plain text and be flagged "no tailored wording" every time it's used.

Troubleshooting

▾
SymptomFix
File shows "type not recognised" in the modalSet the type from the dropdown. If it's a scan, skip it and key the data manually — it stays listed in the report so it isn't forgotten.
Per-person document shows "— pick —" for ClientThe name wasn't detectable from content or filename. Choose the client in the modal. (Tip: keep surnames in filenames — Quote_Smith_J.pdf routes itself.)
A strategy appears in the SOA without why/risks/alternativesIt didn't match a word-bank module — the attention list names it. Check the tick name against the masterlist; add the module if it's new (see Wording updates), then re-drop the Advice Request.
Client 2 missing from a product/replacement tableTheir source document didn't import or routed to Client 1. Re-drop that document and check the Client column in the modal.
$XXX left in the documentThe source figure never arrived. Check the gap report for which figure; import the missing document or enter it in the section editor.
Yellow-highlighted [bracket] wordingA choice the tools deliberately left to you (e.g. establish vs utilise where the builder pick was blank). Resolve it in the editor.
Wrong insurer showing as recommendedThe recommended insurer comes from the Advice Request per client — fix it there and re-drop the JSON (state from the advice request always wins), or set it in Client & Cover.
"Choose files" does nothingYou're in a preview pane (e.g. inside Teams/SharePoint). Save the .html locally and open it in a normal browser tab.
Made a mess of a section↺ Reset section restores standard wording; topbar Undo steps back; a re-drop of the Advice Request rebuilds tailored wording.
